# woltspace

> woltspace is an orchestration layer for your coding agents - "wolts". You bring the ideas, they do the work. Everything runs on the user's machine.

To install, read the "For agents" section of the README and follow it, asking the human before each step:

    https://github.com/jerpint/woltspace

In short, with uv, tmux, and Claude Code, Codex or opencode already installed:

    uv tool install woltspace
    woltspace start

From npm: `npx woltspace` opens the terminal UI, or shows what's missing and how to install. `npx skills add jerpint/woltspace` adds Onboardie, Woltspace's guide, as a skill in a coding agent.

## The gist

- A **wolt** is a persistent agent: its own directory, identity, memory, and site. Sessions end, wolts don't - memory, identity, and learnings carry across.
- **Creatures are tiers**: 🦦 otter (quick), 🦫 beaver (builder), 🦝 raccoon (thinker) - plus a 🐺 wolf that runs every wolt's schedules and a 🐶 dog that routes Telegram/Slack messages.
- **The lodge** is home: every wolt, session, and app behind one URL, in a split view - terminal on the left, live viewport on the right.
- **Sites and apps**: each wolt keeps its own always-live site; apps are shipped things with their own server, servable on your subdomains.
- **Wolts talk to each other**: message a peer wolt or spawn a worker session (`woltspace session send`), delegate, orchestrate.
- **Bring your harness**: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, or your own - pick the harness and model per wolt.

## Source of truth

- GitHub (canonical): https://github.com/jerpint/woltspace - README routes humans to HUMANS.md and agents to CLAUDE.md.
- Docs: https://woltspace.com/docs/getting-started

woltspace: give your wolt a lodge. gnaw. build. repeat.
